assumptions: The first commercial use would be research or validation and would not involve an unauthorized diagnostic claim.
Qualified clinical, laboratory, ethics, legal, and security partners can be engaged without exceeding the stated capital and time constraints.
Participants and relevant institutions would grant explicit, purpose-specific authority for each recontact, collection, and permitted use.
No existing proprietary cohort, customer commitment, or preferred institutional access is available to the founder.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed paid pilot or strong buyer commitment, protocol-specific legal and ethics analysis, participant recruitment and retention costs, qualified partner terms, and demonstrated customer preference over existing CRO or biobank options.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A consent-governed, recontactable cohort can answer prospective measurement and follow-up questions that static datasets cannot, but the insight remains broad until anchored to one phenotype and validation protocol.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: External validation is a real development gate and delay can be costly, yet there is no evidence that a specific developer will pay for this panel, at the proposed price, instead of using a CRO, biobank, or institution.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Protocol fees and lawful reuse could support attractive revenue, but recruitment, participant compensation, laboratory work, governance, secure processing, and customer-specific analysis make both first-study margin and repeat-license economics unproven.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: The potential buyer set spans several well-funded health-technology categories, but no narrow phenotype, buyer segment, reachable account list, or evidence of an underserved initial market is specified.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: CROs, hospitals, laboratories, biobanks, and emerging EHDS access channels have larger cohorts and established governance; a small new panel has no demonstrated route to dominate even a narrow validation niche.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: If one cohort becomes scientifically credible and economically reusable, follow-up intervals, new biomarkers, model versions, subgroups, and adjacent cohorts create meaningful expansion paths.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Longitudinal engagement, consent provenance, phenotype consistency, and study metadata can compound, but permissions are purpose-specific, nonexclusive, and withdrawable, limiting durable control over the underlying asset.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The founder's neuroscience and data-science fit supports quality and analysis, but it does not confer participant access, specimens, clinical partners, approvals, or a proprietary cohort today.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: IVDR performance-evidence needs and more structured health-data access create momentum, although EHDS may also increase the supply of governed alternatives and implementation remains case-specific.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: CRO, laboratory, research-institution, and regulatory-consultant referrals are plausible routes to buyers at a validation gate, but none is contracted and each may prefer to own the customer relationship.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The plan combines participant recruitment, scientific validity, ethics, sensitive-data security, laboratory operations, and long enterprise sales within a limited capital and founder-time envelope; multiple external approvals precede delivery.

highest_value_structural_change: Define one narrow phenotype and secure a partner-backed, prepaid validation protocol in which the same prospectively consented panel has an explicit lawful path to at least one follow-up use.
main_structural_strength: A genuinely recontactable longitudinal cohort could supply prospective measurements and follow-up evidence that static health datasets cannot provide.
primary_score_limiter: The venture controls none of the participant relationships, specimens, institutional permissions, or validation demand on which its proposed asset depends.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established CROs, biobanks, hospitals, laboratories, and EHDS access mechanisms can offer larger governed datasets, while consent withdrawal and protocol-specific authority constrain reuse.
